chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
“The one who has washed the deceased performs ghusl, and everyone who touches a dead body must perform ghusl, even if the deceased has already been washed.”

Because what this report contains in his statement, “even if the deceased has already been washed,” is to be understood as a kind of recommendation rather than obligation, due to the reports we mentioned earlier, and that if he touches him after the ghusl, then no ghusl is required of him.

key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation; an act regarded as meritorious but not obligatory
key_terms.مَسَّ: touched physical contact with the dead body
key_terms.يَغْتَسِلُ: he performs ghusl; the act of ritual bathing being prescribed

ai.seo_question: Is ghusl obligatory after touching a deceased person who has already been washed?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of ghusl for one who washes or touches a deceased person. The appended explanation clarifies that the phrase about touching the deceased after the deceased has already been washed is interpreted as recommended, not obligatory, based on other reports.
